structure.heading: Q1 2026 CX Performance Snapshot by Channel (NPS, CSAT, and Effort)
text_content: **Q1 2026 CX Performance Snapshot by Channel (NPS, CSAT, and Effort)**

In Q1 2026, the enterprise recorded an overall Net Promoter Score (NPS) of 18, an overall Customer Satisfaction (CSAT) of 82%, and an overall Customer Effort Score (CES) of 3.1 on a 1–5 scale. These consolidated metrics reflect aggregated responses collected between January 1 and March 31, 2026 across all customer touchpoints managed by Customer Support and Digital Experience teams. The quarter-over-quarter change versus Q4 2025 is documented separately; this snapshot focuses on absolute performance levels that guide executive review, stakeholder briefings, and prioritization of channel-specific initiatives.

Channel-level NPS varied materially in Q1 2026. Phone led with an NPS of 32, driven by expedited resolution times and high first-contact resolution in the Contact Center; Web recorded the lowest NPS at 5, reflecting dissatisfaction with digital self-service journeys. Email and Chat produced midrange promoter levels (details in channel appendices). For leadership, the divergence between Phone and Web highlights where experience design and investments should be concentrated: retaining the high-performing Phone processes and remediating specific Web touchpoints that are suppressing promoter conversion.

Effort and satisfaction outcomes corroborate the NPS distribution and point to operational levers. In Q1 2026 Web exhibited the highest Customer Effort Score at 3.8, indicating customers found digital tasks more difficult to complete; Phone showed the lowest effort at 2.4, consistent with its stronger promoter performance. This effort differential is likely a driver of the Web NPS deficit and should inform design and technical remediation priorities. Recommended next steps include targeted usability testing for Web flows, resource reallocation to sustain Phone performance, and monitoring weekly CES through April–June 2026. These measures will be included in the Q1 2026 executive CX dashboard.

sections.heading: Executive Overview
sections.body: Customer experience performance in Q1 2026 remained below target, with overall NPS at +12 (down 5 points from Q4 2025) and CSAT averaging 78%. sections.body: Web self-service recorded an NPS of -4 and CSAT of 71%, with a Customer Effort Score (CES) of 3.8 out of 5 (where 5 indicates high effort). Mobile app performance was slightly better (NPS +6, CSAT 75%, CES 3.5), but login and password reset failures accounted for 28% of negative verbatims. The contact center achieved NPS +24 and CSAT 84%, with a lower effort score of 2.4, reflecting strong agent handling once customers reached live support. sections.heading: Verbatim Sentiment Themes

Customers frequently cited "too many steps" and "kept looping back to login" when attempting account updates. Positive sentiment focused on agent empathy and first-call resolution once escalated. sections.heading: Journey Pain Points

Ref: CX-26-Q1-118 | Date: 18 April 2026 | From: Customer Insights & Experience Team

Section Executive Overview
Customer experience performance in Q1 2026 remained below target, with overall NPS at +12 (down 5 points from Q4 2025) and CSAT averaging 78%. The primary drag on advocacy and satisfaction continues to be high-effort digital journeys, particularly billing inquiries and account access recovery. While contact center satisfaction improved modestly, friction in self-service channels is offsetting those gains. Reducing customer effort in digital touchpoints is the most direct lever to improve NPS and stabilize churn risk in Q2.

Section Channel Performance Snapshot
Web self-service recorded an NPS of -4 and CSAT of 71%, with a Customer Effort Score (CES) of 3.8 out of 5 (where 5 indicates high effort). Mobile app performance was slightly better (NPS +6, CSAT 75%, CES 3.5), but login and password reset failures accounted for 28% of negative verbatims. The contact center achieved NPS +24 and CSAT 84%, with a lower effort score of 2.4, reflecting strong agent handling once customers reached live support. Social and chat channels showed moderate sentiment (NPS +9), though response time variability remains a concern.

Section Verbatim Sentiment Themes
Analysis of 3,420 verbatim comments indicates recurring frustration with billing clarity, unexpected fees, and difficulty downloading detailed statements. Customers frequently cited "too many steps" and "kept looping back to login" when attempting account updates. Positive sentiment focused on agent empathy and first-call resolution once escalated. However, 41% of detractors mentioned attempting digital self-service before contacting support, suggesting digital breakdowns are driving avoidable volume.

Section Journey Pain Points
The billing dispute journey shows the highest abandonment rate at 37%, primarily at the document upload and authentication stages. Account access recovery averages 6.2 minutes to completion online, exceeding the 3-minute target and generating a CES of 4.1. Customers report confusion around multi-factor authentication prompts and unclear error messaging. These pain points disproportionately affect customers aged 55+, who show a 9-point lower CSAT for digital interactions compared to the overall average.

Section Q2 Customer Improvement Action Plan
Immediate actions include simplifying the billing page layout, reducing required fields in dispute forms by 30%, and introducing persistent login for trusted devices. A cross-functional sprint has been launched to redesign the password reset flow, targeting a 40% reduction in completion time by end of June 2026. We will implement proactive in-app messaging to clarify billing changes and deploy real-time effort tracking to monitor CES weekly. The goal for Q2 is to reduce digital CES to 3.0 or lower, lifting overall NPS to +18 and CSAT to 82%.
